Tests for {@link UnicodeEscaper}, which escapes selected code points into their {@code \\uXXXX} Unicode representation.

The behaviour under test depends on how the escaper is configured:

  • {@code new UnicodeEscaper()} / {@code between(low, high)} escape code points that fall inside the inclusive range.
  • {@code outsideOf(low, high)} / {@code above(x)} / {@code below(x)} escape code points that fall outside the exclusive range.

{@code translate} returns {@code true} (and writes the escape) when the code point is escaped, and {@code false} (writing nothing) when it is left untouched.
The default escaper escapes every code point. Integer.MAX_VALUE is above 0xFFFF, so it is escaped via the multi-digit hex form "\\u7FFFFFFF".
above(571) escapes any code point greater than 571. The code point 629 (0x0275) qualifies and is escaped as "\\u0275".
between(low, high) only escapes code points inside the inclusive range. -2931 falls below the [-2014, -2014] range, so it is left untouched.
outsideOf(1151, 91) escapes code points outside the exclusive range, i.e. below 1151 or above 91. The code point 629 (0x0275) is below 1151 and so is escaped as "\\u0275".
between(55296, 1166) has its low boundary above its high boundary, so the inclusive range is empty. The code point 55296 satisfies neither bound and is therefore left untouched.

below(0) escapes code points below 0. Translating the CharSequence "5F8" starts at code point '5' (0x35), which is not below 0, so nothing is escaped and the writer receives the original text unchanged.
